title: A good day
hook: Yunmen asks his monks about the days to come, and when no one answers, he answers for them
tomorrow: why did a Roman wait for the lamp to go out each night?

segments.voice: Yesterday was the tired version: when there's nothing left, one breath still counts. Today is the other kind of day, the one that went fine, and a teacher who had something to say about it.
screen: `ONE BREATH.` → `AND THE DAY THAT WENT FINE?`

segments.voice: How was your day? Fine. Nothing broke, nothing big happened. Hardly an answer at all. In a Zen hall in China, a teacher named Yunmen once asked his monks a question about days. He said: I'm not asking you about the days before the fifteenth. Tell me something about the days after the fifteenth. The hall went quiet. Nobody had an answer. So Yunmen answered for them.
screen: `HOW WAS YOUR DAY? FINE.` → `YUNMEN ASKS ABOUT THE DAYS AHEAD.` → `THE HALL GOES QUIET.`

segments.voice: His answer: every day is a good day. The exchange is kept in the Blue Cliff Record, a Chinese collection of Zen teaching stories, as case six. Here's what makes it strange. Yunmen doesn't say every day is pleasant, or lucky, or easy. Some readers hear the fifteenth as the full moon, a marker in the month, so the question becomes: what about every day from here on? And the answer refuses to sort days into good and bad at all. That is the Zen teaching handed down with the line: a day isn't good because of what it gave you. It's good because it's the one that's actually here, and you are in it. So a good day isn't a verdict at bedtime, a score out of ten. It's an attention you bring with you. Which means naming what made today good isn't a gratitude trick. It's a way of checking whether you were there for it. A laugh at the bus stop. Warm bread. A small hand in yours at the crosswalk.
screen: `EVERY DAY IS A GOOD DAY.` · `THE BLUE CLIFF RECORD, CASE SIX.` · `NOT LUCKY. NOT EASY. HERE.` · `ATTENTION, NOT A SCORE.` · then, large: `A GOOD DAY.`

segments.voice: Sit easy and let today run back through you, from waking until now. Stop on one small thing that was good, and name it out loud, softly, in a few plain words: the coffee, the light on the wall, a text from a friend. Then breathe with it until the bell.
A good day: in Yunmen's sense, not a lucky day, but this one, met while you're actually in it.
Keep this one: a good day is any day you were there for. See you tomorrow.
